newsitem.title: POLAND: Floods recede in Poland, cabinet mulls relief bonds.
newsitem.headline: Floods recede in Poland, cabinet mulls relief bonds.

text.p: Flood waters eased further in Poland on Monday and the government said it would consider issuing special bonds next year to help finance reconstruction of the ravaged southwestern regions.
People in the town of Slubice on the German border, where authorities ordered mass evacuation at the weekend because of the surging river Odra, were desperately fighting to maintain eroded dikes.
"The flood situation is stabilising. Slubice has so far resisted the river... but the fight to save the sodden dikes continues," said crisis committee spokesman Krzysztof Pomes.
The town, across the river from Frankfurt an der Oder, may still face a renewed threat of total flooding when a second water surge on the Odra reaches the area in several days, he said.
Independent analysts say the floods, which killed 55 people, destroyed many roads, bridges and buildings and wrought damages of up to 7.5 billion zlotys ($2.2 billion).
Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said the government would consider issuing special bonds next year to raise funds for reconstruction of inundated areas.
He rejected a proposal of the biggest opposition group, the Solidarity Election Action (AWS), to issue the bonds, which are to be deducted from personal income tax, as early as this year.

"At the moment we see no urgent need to gather additional means to finance these activities (reconstructing the flooded regions)," he told reporters after a meeting of the government's National Programme of Reconstruction and Modernisation Council.

"We have considered...the flood bonds... They could be used if, during works on (next year's) budget draft, it turns out that it is necessary to supplement the sources of financing the reconstruction."
The flood crisis committee said on Monday that about 2,000 sq km (750 square miles) remained under water while 403 towns and villages were inundated, 47 completely.

It said more than 100,000 troops, firefighters, policeman and boreder guards were engaged in the rescue operations. People were coming back to their homes as water retreated, but nearly 40,000 remained displaced.

The government has earmarked some 650 million zlotys for flood relief which it squeezed from the 1997 budget. It also plans to borrow about $600 million from the World Bank and the European Investment Bank (EIB).

As an emergency measure, parliament has authorised the government to borrow an additional 2.5 billion zlotys ($728 million) from the National Bank of Poland this year, of which one billion zlotys has already been drawn.
The AWS, the main challenger of Cimoszewicz's ex-communist party in parliamentary elections on September 21, has said the government plan to borrow money from the central bank would stir inflation.
"Issuing the flood bonds would help avoid more inflation," AWS deputy head Janusz Tomszewski said.
The central bank has said the government is likely to slightly overshoot its 13 percent inflation target for December this year. ($ = 3.445 Polish Zlotys)
